Before I travel to meet a local team, my analysts have already read everything that is public: the contract, the regulator's decisions, the news. So I do not need a long presentation. In the first meeting I ask three questions. What has already been approved? What has not happened yet? And what has changed in the last month? A team that answers those three questions in ten minutes gets a second meeting. We have just finished a process in Chile, and the team there did exactly that. They even sent the minutes before I got back to the hotel.

I have worked with foreign funds for about fifteen years, and I have learned one thing. When an investor pushes back, do not argue in the room. Last year we had a client who wanted to defend every point of the term sheet. After two meetings, nobody had moved. In the third meeting we changed the approach. We agreed on the facts first, we wrote them on the board, and we checked that everybody was on the same page. The deal has not closed yet, but the discussion is much faster now, and the fund has already asked for a new draft.
